Learning Objective: Identify common nouns representing everyday objects in a room.
Instructional Text / Examples: Look around you! Everything you can touch and see has a name. Words that name people, places, or things are called nouns. Today, we are focusing on things, which we call 'objects'. For example: desk, pencil, book, chair, and blackboard.
Interactive Prompt / Assessment: Look around your current room. Write down 3 objects you can see right now that are nouns.

Learning Objective: Understand the difference between one object (singular) and more than one object (plural) by adding '-s' or '-es'.
Instructional Text / Examples: When we talk about only ONE object, it is singular (e.g., 'one apple'). When we talk about TWO or more objects, it is plural. To make most nouns plural, we just add '-s' to the end of the word. Example: 1 book -> 2 books. If a word ends in ch, sh, x, s, or z, we add '-es'. Example: 1 box -> 3 boxes.
Interactive Prompt / Assessment: Change these singular objects into plural objects: 1) pencil -> ___, 2) brush -> ___.

Learning Objective: Use descriptive words (adjectives) to give more detail about common objects.
Instructional Text / Examples: We can make our writing more interesting by describing our objects! Words that describe nouns are called adjectives. Adjectives tell us about size, color, shape, or how something feels. Example: 'The shiny red apple.' Here, 'shiny' and 'red' are adjectives describing the object 'apple'.
Interactive Prompt / Assessment: Find the adjective in this sentence: 'Timmy dropped his heavy backpack on the floor.' Which word describes the backpack?

Learning Objective: Combine nouns and adjectives to form complete, grammatically correct sentences about objects.
Instructional Text / Examples: A complete sentence always starts with a capital letter, ends with punctuation (like a period), and makes complete sense. When writing about objects, we combine our noun and adjective. Example: 'The yellow pencil is sharp.'
Interactive Prompt / Assessment: Fix this broken sentence: 'small the cat found a blue ball' (Hint: Fix capitalization, order, and punctuation!)
